parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish اسطال (astal, “dining table”), itself from Hungarian asztal (“table, desk”).
From Ottoman Turkish حیدود (haydut), from Hungarian hajdúk. Doublet of hödük (“boor, peasant”).

parole.significato: boor, peasant, lout, an uncouth or crude person
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish هودوك (hödük, “boor, peasant”), itself from Hungarian hajdúk (“armed cattle-drover; hajduk”). Doublet of haydut (“brigand, bandit”).

Inherited from Ottoman Turkish قوپچه (ḳopça, “a hook-and-eye”), from Hungarian kapocs (“hook, clamp, clip, buckle”). Cognates with Albanian kopsë, Bulgarian ко́пче (kópče), Gagauz kopça, Greek κόπιτσα (kópitsa), Northern Kurdish qopçe, Macedonian копче (kopče), Russian кнопка (knopka), Serbo-Croatia

parole.significato: palanka (a permanently entrenched camp attached to Turkish frontier fortresses)
parole.testo: From Ottoman Turkish پلانقه (palanka), from Hungarian palánk, from Latin phalanga. Doublet of palanga.
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish صالاش or صلاش (ṣalaş, “a booth”), from Hungarian szállás.
From Ottoman Turkish صوبا (soba), borrowed from Hungarian szoba, from Old High German stuba, from Proto-West Germanic *stubu. Doublet of izbe.
From Ottoman Turkish طابور (tabur). According to Nişanyan, the Ottoman Turkish term is from Hungarian tábor, which itself is from Chagatai [Term?].
From Ottoman Turkish واروش, from Hungarian város (“city, town”).

parole.significato: shabrack, the saddlecloth formerly used by European light cavalry
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish چاپراق (çaprak, “shabrack”), from Hungarian csáprág.

parole.significato: stockade, palisade, an enclosure protected by a wall of wooden posts
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish شرانپول (şaranpol, “stockade, palisade”), itself from Hungarian sorompó (“boom barrier, boom gate”).
